## `Ali_3801_Globo_DVBT_dump SPI 4mb.bin`

* **Box:** Globo STB HD N3
* **Type:** DVB-T set-top box
* **SoC:** ALi M3801 (M3801)
* **Demodulator:** internal (NIM_S3811)
* **Tuner:** Rafael Micro R820T (7-bit I2C address 0x1A, 0x34 as the write address byte, on the first hardware I2C master)
* **Flash:** 4 MB SPI (desoldered and read with a programmer)
* **Front panel:** TM1650 (SCL 31, SDA 9)
* **IR coding:** nec
* **Image:** dump, maincode "M3801 DVBT" 2014-6-23 (name 406000000003002), 2014-06-23, 4194304 bytes, SHA-1 ef46dee13875ce21193b9ffe58c031aebd83c54b
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000, HDCPKey 0x04FE00, maincode 0x050000, Radioback 0x290000, defaultdb 0x2A0000, userdb 0x2BFF80 -- the dump_maciej.bin layout and maincode name
* **Source:** [elektroda.pl](https://www.elektroda.pl/rtvforum/topic4156384-30.html#21933067), JacekTorun (2026-07-05) -- login needed. Thread "Jak skompilować i uruchomić własny firmware dla ALI M3801 i innych układów z tunerów?", page 2, post #40 (machine translation: https://www.elektroda.com/rtvforum/topic4156384-30.html#21933067)
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes, panel ' ON '. Keeps its channel list, so the application tunes a channel at start, shows a channel banner that times out and then its no-signal message (run_dump_globo_capture_screen.py).  With sim.set_signal(True) -- the R820T model and the internal demodulator's lock -- the tuner calibrates and locks at the first try and the no-signal box never appears (run_dump_globo_signal.py).

Tuner: a Rafael Micro R820T on the chip's first hardware I2C master (0xB8018200, i2c_scb.py) at 7-bit address 0x1A (0x34 as the write address byte): when the application tunes its first channel (about 93 M instructions in) it writes the R820T initialisation array -- registers 0x05..0x1F = 83 32 75 C0 40 D6 6C F5 53 75 68 6C 83 80 00 0F 00 C0 30 48 CC 60 00 54 A6 4A C0, the public R820T driver's bytes but for two values -- then runs the filter and image calibrations (5- and 2-byte reads: the Rafael read protocol starts at register 0 and sends every byte bit-reversed) and its PLL, whose lock it checks in register 2 with a 3-byte read; on no lock it raises the VCO current (0x12: 0x88 -> 0x68) exactly like the Linux r820t driver.  The demodulator is the chip's own ("NIM_S3811_0").

The driver is Rafael's R828 reference code (its DVB-T 8 MHz standard: IF 4570 kHz, filter calibration at 63 MHz) with a 16 MHz crystal -- the constant of its image-rejection ring loop, (16+n)*8*16000 >= 3100000, at 0x8025E628; the NIM's own tuner configuration holds the generic PLL-tuner defaults (4 MHz, divider 24, step 166 kHz).  With the R820T model the whole sequence decodes: image-rejection calibration at five ring points (LO 528.0, 194.7, 61.4, 394.7 and 794.7 MHz: 3.2 GHz / 6, 16, 48, 8, 4 minus 5.3 MHz) with the antenna input off, the filter calibration at 63 MHz, then the channel "41. WP": LO 203.070 MHz, RF 198.500 MHz -- VHF channel 8 -- about 117 M instructions in.

UART log of the real box from the same post (the forum collapses repeated spaces and shows "@" before a domain-like word as "(_at_)"):

APP init! / bl_panel_init! / bl_flash_init! / bl_verify_sw / success! / MC: APP init ok / << SDK4.0ba.4.0_20101217 >> / Libcore version 8.13.0(_at_)SDK4.0bd.8.13_20130731(gcc version 3.4.4 mipssde-6.06.01-20070420)(Vic.Wang@ Thu Aug 1 15:38:18 2013) / Application version 1.0.0(_at_)SDK4.0ba.7.4_20120227

## `AMIKO ALI3606/ALI3606_0A010A00_gui_edision_1.6.89.abs`

* **Box:** Amiko Mini HD / SHD-8140 (System ID 0A010A00, Edision GUI 1.6.89 build)
* **Type:** DVB-S2 Full HD satellite receiver with CA card reader and Ethernet
* **Board:** 0A010A00 (Synaps / GiGaBlue / Edision / Amiko M3606 platform)
* **SoC:** ALi M3606 / C3603 (the main-code chunk's version "M3606 ", the seecode chunk's "M3606 SEE"; Libcore 7.24.0@SDK4.0ba.7.24_SAB_20130620) (M3602 (chips/m3602.py), matched by the main-code chunk's version)
* **Demodulator:** internal (NIM_S3501_0)
* **Flash:** 8 MB SPI
* **IR coding:** necfirst
* **Image:** update, 1.6.89 (maincode "M3606 " 2015-10-20; bootloader << SDK4.0ba.4.0_20101217 >>; Libcore 7.24.0@SDK4.0ba.7.24_SAB_20130620), 2015-10-20, 8388608 bytes, SHA-1 484d8fb9dbe40d6c25c63b613582e3dc55f62e3c
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000 (M3606A 1.1.3), maincode 0x020000 (0A010A001689), seecode 0x320000 (M3606 SEE), default_lang 0x46FD00 (1.0.0), cipluskey 0x46FF80 (1.1.0), cipluskey 0x480000 (1.0.0), logo 0x488000 (1.0.0), Menuback 0x498000 (1.0.0), BootLogo 0x4B8000 (1.0.0), Radioback 0x4D8000 (1.0.0), patch 0x4FFF80 (1.0.0), defaultdb 0x520000 (1.0.1), userdb 0x73FF80 (1.0.1)
* **Source:** [satedu.cba.pl (a mirror of the official download)](http://www.satedu.cba.pl/index.php?action=downloadfile&filename=ALI3606_0A010A00_gui_edision_1.6.89.rar&directory=Firmware%20for%20to%20all%20receivers/Amiko/Amiko%20inne), Amiko / Edision (2015-10-20). Archive ALI3606_0A010A00_gui_edision_1.6.89.rar from the Amiko / Amiko inne directory on satedu.cba.pl; fetched 2026-10-18.
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes. Boots as the M3602 family with device.chipId 0x3603 (C3603): the bootloader at 0x000000 (whose chunk header has next = 0, followed at length + 0x80 = 0x020000 by maincode; chips/base.py:chunk_chain) reads the 8 MB flash via SPI quad I/O read 0xEB, unpacks the 9.3 MB maincode into RAM and starts it.  With _find_long_blocks breaking an unrolled crypto routine in maincode so Unicorn 2.1.4's TCG buffer does not overflow, the application starts the SEE co-processor ("M3606 SEE"), initialises the S3501 demodulator at I2C 0x33, and renders its 32-bpp ARGB8888 OSD (8 GE commands, 10 unique colours; without the board's encrypted anti-clone security IC at SCB I2C 0x10 it displays "SW is not designed for this HW, please change back to official SW! -----0a010a00 00000000").  Its 54-key remote table (0x44xx) uses the "necfirst" coding.

Amiko ALI3606 (System ID 0A010A00) firmware 1.6.89 with the Edision HD GUI (2015-10-20) on an 8 MB SPI flash.

Built on the ALi M3606 / C3603 dual-core SDK (Libcore 7.24.0@SDK4.0ba.7.24_SAB_20130620) shared across Amiko and Edision receivers; silences UART TX via a dummy printf stub and checks an external anti-clone crypto chip at I2C 0x10 at startup.


## `AMIKO CHD8270+/amiko_14000A00_galaxy_2.4.89_gisclub.tv.abs`

* **Box:** Amiko CHD8270+ (System ID 14000A00, v2.3.40 EMU build)
* **Type:** DVB-C / DVB-T2 Full HD Twin Cable/Terrestrial receiver with Conax / MultiCAS card reader, CI+ slot, Ethernet and USB PVR

* **Front panel:** tm1650 (SCL 135, SDA 134)
* **IR coding:** necfirst

Archive amiko_14000A00_galaxy_2.4.89_gisclub.tv.abs from AMIKO CHD8270+; added for expanded coverage.
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes, panel ' ON ' -> ' on '. Boots as M3503 rev B with 256 MB DDR3 (chips/m3503.py, run_dump_chd8270_plus_app_starts.py, run_dump_chd8270_plus_capture_screen.py): the XIP bootloader ("M3516A 1.2.1") runs with CacheAsRam at 0x8FFF8000..0x8FFFFFFF, prints "CH455 panel init OK!" and writes " ON " to the CH455 front panel on GPIO 135 (SCL) / 134 (SDA), parks the SEE boot stub at 0xA14187DC, unpacks seecode ("M3606 SEE") to 0xAE000200 and maincode(AV) to 0x80000200, and starts both cores (EBase 0x80002000 / 0x8E002001).  The application prints "hs_config_init", updates the CH455 display to " on ", populates userdb(64+64) at 0xF3FF80, and draws its 1280x720 OSD dialog on GMA layer 0 (9 GE commands, 4 colours).

Amiko CHD8270+ (System ID 14000A00) firmware v2.3.40 EMU (2016-01-15) on a 16 MB SPI flash for the ALi M3516A / M3503 rev B Full HD DVB-C / DVB-T2 Cable/Terrestrial CI+ receiver with 256 MB DDR3.

Pairs dual-CPU M3503 maincode + seecode ("M3606 SEE" at 0xAE000200) with a CH455 4-digit LED panel on GPIO 135 / 134 (" ON " -> " on ") and a 60-entry 0x60xx remote control table ("necfirst" coding).

The application initialises its external Availink AVL6762 DVB-T2/C demodulator at I2C 0x14 over bit-banged GPIO I2C on SCL = GPIO 7 / SDA = GPIO 8 ("Demod is 6762!!!", demods.py:AVL6762) and Airoha AV2012 DVB-S2 tuner at I2C 0x61 on SCB0, drives the CH455 front panel on GPIO 135 / 134 (" ON ", " on "), populates userdb(64+64) at 0xF3FF80, and renders its 1920x1080 CLUT8 OSD through GeM36F / GMA layer 0 (without the board's anti-clone security IC it displays the hardware-ID warning dialog).

Amiko HD8260+ (System ID 14000A00 / 14000A88) firmware v.2468 with the Edision Piccollo GUI (2019-01-25) for the Full HD DVB-S2 + DVB-T2/C combo receiver on the ALi M3516A / M3503 SoC with 256 MB DDR3 and a 16 MB SPI flash.

Pairs the M3516A's internal DVB-S2 front-end + Airoha AV2012 tuner (0x61 on SCB0) with an external Availink AVL6762 DVB-T2/C demodulator at 0x14 on bit-banged GPIO 7 / 8 + MaxLinear MxL608 tuner (0x60), and drives a CH455 4-digit LED panel on GPIO 135 / 134.

Amiko HD8265+ (System ID 6C000A00) firmware v.1529 with the Edision GUI (2020-12-20) for the Full HD H.265/HEVC DVB-S2 + DVB-T2/C combo receiver on the ALi M3529A / C3505 SoC with 256 MB DDR3 and 8 MB SPI flash.

## `AMIKO HD9265+/Amiko_HD9265+_1.0.10_emu.abs`

* **Box:** Amiko HD9265+ (System ID 8E000A00, v1.0.10 EMU build)
* **Type:** DVB-S2X + DVB-T2/C Full HD H.265/HEVC combo receiver with CI+ slot, Conax CA card reader, Gigabit Ethernet and USB Wi-Fi
* **Board:** 8E000A00 (bootloader version "M3759A 1.0.1", 8 MB SPI flash, ALi C3702 / CAP210 ARMv7-A platform)
* **SoC:** ALi M3759A / C3702 (ARMv7-A Cortex-A9 CPU, get_clock_cap210 / get_clock_3702, DECV_HEVC_0/1, NIM_C3501h_0 + Availink AVL6862) (M3801 (chips/m3801.py, NCRC chunk container only; CPU is ARMv7-A rather than MIPS32))
* **Demodulator:** internal DVB-S2X (NIM_C3501h_0) + external Availink AVL6862 DVB-T2/C
* **Tuner:** Airoha AV20xx (Av20xxTuner_type)
* **Flash:** 8 MB SPI
* **IR coding:** nec
* **Image:** update, 1.0.10 EMU (maincode(AV) "8E000A001010"; bootloader "M3759A 1.0.1", 2019-08-24), 2019-08-24, 8388608 bytes, SHA-1 003fc0027db4442d519e875debdfff184e158c07
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000 (M3759A 1.0.1, 2019-08-24), maincode(AV) 0x078000 (8E000A001010, 2010-08-12, LZMA -> 15.31 MB), default_lang 0x53FD00 (1.0.0), cipluskey 0x53FF80 (1.1.0), countryband 0x54FF80 (1.0.0), img_webserver 0x557F80 (1.0.0), patch 0x5B7F80 (1.0.0), logo_user 0x647F80 (1.0.0), logo_menu 0x657F80 (1.0.0), logo_radio 0x677F80 (1.0.0), logo_boot 0x697F80 (1.0.0), patch 0x6BFF80 (1.0.0), defaultdb(PRC) 0x6E0000 (1.0.1), userdb(64+64) 0x73FF80 (1.0.1)
* **Source:** [satedu.cba.pl (a mirror of the Amiko firmware archive)](http://www.satedu.cba.pl/index.php?action=downloadfile&filename=Amiko_HD9265_1.0.10_emu.zip&directory=Firmware%20for%20to%20all%20receivers/Amiko), Amiko (2019-08-24). Archive Amiko_HD9265_1.0.10_emu.zip from the Amiko directory on satedu.cba.pl; fetched 2026-11-04.
* **Simulator:** boots no, application no, display no. Does not boot on the MIPS32 simulator (run_dump_hd9265_1010_emu_arm_layout.py): although the 8 MB image uses ALi's standard NCRC chunk chain (magic 0x23010010 at 0x000000, HEAD descriptor at 0x250, LZMA-compressed maincode(AV) "8E000A001010" at 0x078000 decompressing to 15.31 MB), the ALi M3759A / C3702 ("get_clock_cap210", "get_clock_3702") is an ARMv7-A (Cortex-A9) SoC rather than MIPS32.  Its boot-ROM payload at 0x800 starts with an 8-word ARMv7 exception vector table (b #0x820; b #0x804; b #0x944; ...) followed at 0x820 by mrc p15, #0, r0, c1, c0, #0 (reading CP15 SCTLR).

Amiko HD9265+ (System ID 8E000A00) firmware v1.0.10 EMU (2019-08-24) for the Full HD H.265/HEVC DVB-S2X + DVB-T2/C CI+ combo receiver on the ALi M3759A / C3702 SoC with 8 MB SPI flash.

Illustrates ALi's transition from MIPS32 (C3503 / C3505) to ARMv7-A (C3702 / CAP210, M3759A) while retaining the identical NCRC chunk header layout, LZMA stream format, and ALi TDS driver naming (CH455_0, NIM_C3501h_0, DECV_HEVC_0).

Boots as a 128 MB DDR3 M3626A / C3505 board (chips/c3505.py, run_dump_impulse_h265_app_starts.py, run_dump_impulse_h265_capture_screen.py): the boot-ROM bootloader runs in boot SRAM at 0x9FE00800, unpacks maincode(AV) (chips/base.py:maincode) to 0x80000200 and seecode ("M3606 SEE") to 0xA6000200, and starts both cores (main EBase 0x80002000, SEE EBase 0x86002001).  The application initialises its external Availink AVL6762 DVB-T2/C demodulator at I2C 0x14 and MaxLinear MxL608 tuner at I2C 0x60 over bit-banged GPIO I2C on SCL = GPIO 105 / SDA = GPIO 104 ("Demod is 6762!!!", tuned to 474.000 MHz / 8 MHz), drives the CH455 front panel on GPIO 107 / 110 (" ON ", " on "), populates its hs_control database, and renders its 1280x720 ARGB8888 OSD through the display engine at 0xB8006900 (5 GE commands, 14 unique colours; without the board's anti-clone security IC it displays the hardware-ID warning dialog "SW is not designed for this HW, please change back to offical SW!-----00000000000000 74000a00", like Amiko HD8155).

Amiko Impulse H.265 T2/C (System ID 74000A00) firmware v1.3.87 emu (2019-06-26) for the Full HD H.265/HEVC DVB-T2/C terrestrial and cable receiver on the ALi M3626A / C3505 SoC with 128 MB DDR3 and 8 MB SPI flash.

Terrestrial/cable counterpart to the Amiko HD8155: pairs an external Availink AVL6762 DVB-T2/C demodulator at 0x14 and MaxLinear MxL608 tuner at 0x60 on bit-banged GPIO 105 / 104 with a CH455 4-digit LED panel on GPIO 107 / 110 and the Amiko 0x60xx remote table ("necfirst" coding).


## `AMIKO IMPULSE SAT/AMIKO_Impulse_SAT_2.3.40_emu.abs`

* **Box:** Amiko Impulse SAT (System ID 20020A00)
* **Type:** DVB-S2 Full HD satellite receiver with Conax / MultiCAS card reader, external IR sensor / 4-digit LED eye, and USB PVR
* **Board:** 20020A00 (bootloader version "M3510B 1.1.1", 128 MB DDR3 M3503 revision B platform)
* **SoC:** ALi M3510B / M3503 rev B (128 MB DDR3 dual-CPU DVB-S2 SoC reading chip ID 0x3503 rev 0x0001; NIM_S3503_0, DMX_S3601_0/2, DECV_AVC_0, DECV_AVS_0, DECV_S3601_0, OSD_M36F_0/1, seecode "M3606 SEE" at 0xA6000200; SDK4.0fa.13.11_20150910 / SDK4.0fa.13.6_20141203byD09WXW) (M3503 (chips/m3503.py))
* **Demodulator:** internal ALi M3503 / M3510B DVB-S2 (NIM_S3503_0 at 0xB8028000)
* **Tuner:** Airoha AV2026 DVB-S2 tuner + ASC RF374 modulator
* **Flash:** 8 MB SPI
* **Front panel:** CH455 (TM1650-compatible) (SCL 135, SDA 134)
* **IR coding:** necfirst
* **Image:** update, 2.3.40 (maincode(AV) "20020A002340"; bootloader "M3510B 1.1.1"; SDK4.0fa.13.11_20150910), 2016-01-15, 8388608 bytes, SHA-1 e13dd6ca84b98f088bd792a7ba85e16e0c7846e0
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000 (M3510B 1.1.1, 2012-12-20, XIP with CacheAsRam stack at 0x8FFF8000), MemCfg 0x02F000 (00000001, 2016-1-15), maincode(AV) 0x030000 (20020A002340, LZMA -> 12.37 MB at 0x80000200), seecode 0x3B0000 (M3606 SEE, 2016-1-15, LZMA -> 2.98 MB at 0xA6000200), default_lang 0x4AFD00, cipluskey 0x4AFF80, countryband 0x4C0000, logo_user 0x4C8000, logo_menu 0x4D8000, logo_radio 0x4F8000, logo_boot 0x518000, patch 0x53FF80, defaultdb(FAC) 0x560000, defaultdb(PRC) 0x5E0000, userdb(64+64) 0x73FF80
* **Source:** [satedu.cba.pl](http://www.satedu.cba.pl/index.php?action=downloadfile&filename=AMIKO_Impulse_SAT_2.3.40_emu.zip&directory=Firmware%20for%20to%20all%20receivers/Amiko/Amiko%20HD), Amiko (2016-01-15). Archive AMIKO_Impulse_SAT_2.3.40_emu.zip from the Amiko / Amiko HD directory on satedu.cba.pl; fetched 2026-11-01.
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes, panel ' ON ' -> ' on '. Boots as a 128 MB M3503 revision B board (chips/m3503.py, run_dump_impulse_sat_app_starts.py, run_dump_impulse_sat_capture_screen.py): the XIP bootloader ("M3510B 1.1.1") runs from flash using CacheAsRam at 0x8FFF8000..0x8FFFFFFF before relocating to DDR, prints "CH455 panel init OK!", writes " ON " to the CH455 panel on GPIO 135 / 134, parks the SEE boot stub at 0xA141A7DC, unpacks seecode ("M3606 SEE", 2.98 MB) and maincode(AV) ("20020A002340", 12.37 MB) to 0x80000200, and starts both cores ("MC: APP  init ok", main EBase 0x80002000, SEE running at 0xA6000200 with EBase 0x86002001).  The application prints "---led 455 attach OK--" and updates the CH455 panel to " on ", initialises hs_config_init and userdb(64+64) from defaultdb(PRC) over SPI, and without the board's anti-clone security IC displays "SW is not designed for this HW, please change back to offical SW!-----00000000000000 20020a00" on GMA layer 0 (1280x720).

Amiko Impulse SAT (System ID 20020A00) firmware v2.3.40 (2016-01-15) for the compact Full HD DVB-S2 satellite receiver on the ALi M3510B / M3503 rev B SoC with 128 MB DDR3 and 8 MB SPI flash.

Uses an XIP CacheAsRam bootloader ("M3510B 1.1.1"), dual-CPU "M3606 SEE" firmware at 0xA6000200, and an external CH455 4-digit LED / IR sensor eye on GPIO 135 (SCL) / 134 (SDA).

* **Type:** DVB-S2 Full HD satellite receiver with Conax / MultiCAS card reader, Ethernet and USB PVR
* **Board:** 20020A88 (bootloader version "M3510B 1.1.1", 8 MB SPI flash, 128 MB DDR3 M3503 revision B platform)
* **SoC:** ALi M3510B / M3503 rev B (128 MB DDR3 dual-CPU DVB-S2 SoC reading chip ID 0x3503 rev 0x0001; seecode "M3606 SEE" at 0xA6000200) (M3503 (chips/m3503.py))
* **Demodulator:** internal ALi M3503 / M3510B DVB-S2 (NIM_S3503_0 at 0xB8028000)
* **Tuner:** Airoha AV2026 DVB-S2 tuner
* **Flash:** 8 MB SPI
* **Front panel:** CH455 (TM1650-compatible) (SCL 135, SDA 134)
* **IR coding:** necfirst
* **Image:** update, 2.4.31 EMU (maincode(AV) "20020A882431"; bootloader "M3510B 1.1.1"; seecode "M3606 SEE"), 2017-11-10, 8388608 bytes, SHA-1 12bb775ea8c3e4b15e490d740e0d070d8a43261e
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000 (M3510B 1.1.1, 2012-12-20), MemCfg 0x02F000 (00000001), maincode(AV) 0x030000 (20020A882431, 2010-08-12, LZMA -> 11.23 MB), seecode 0x3B0000 (M3606 SEE, 2017-11-10), default_lang 0x4AFD00 (1.0.0), cipluskey 0x4AFF80 (1.1.0), countryband 0x4C0000 (1.0.0), logo_user 0x4C8000 (1.0.0), logo_menu 0x4D8000 (1.0.0), logo_radio 0x4F8000 (1.0.0), logo_boot 0x518000 (1.0.0), patch 0x53FF80 (1.0.0), defaultdb(PRC) 0x560000 (1.0.1), userdb(64+64) 0x73FF80 (1.0.1)
* **Source:** [satedu.cba.pl](http://www.satedu.cba.pl/index.php?action=downloadfile&filename=AMIKO_Impulse_SAT_2.4.31_emu.zip&directory=Firmware%20for%20to%20all%20receivers/Amiko/Amiko%20HD), Amiko (2017-11-10). Archive AMIKO_Impulse_SAT_2.4.31_emu.zip from the Amiko / Amiko HD directory on satedu.cba.pl; fetched 2026-11-04.
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes, panel ' ON ' -> ' on '. Boots as a 128 MB M3503 revision B board (chips/m3503.py, run_dump_impulse_sat_2431_app_starts.py, run_dump_impulse_sat_2431_capture_screen.py): the XIP bootloader ("M3510B 1.1.1") runs from flash using CacheAsRam at 0x8FFF8000..0x8FFFFFFF, prints "CH455 panel init OK!", writes " ON " to the CH455 panel on GPIO 135 / 134, parks the SEE boot stub at 0xA141A7DC, unpacks seecode ("M3606 SEE") to 0xA6000200 and maincode(AV) ("20020A882431", 11.23 MB) to 0x80000200, and starts both cores (main EBase 0x80002000, SEE EBase 0x86002001).  The application updates the CH455 panel to " on ", populates userdb(64+64) from defaultdb(PRC) over SPI, and renders its 1280x720 OSD dialog on GMA layer 0.

Amiko Impulse SAT (System ID 20020A88) firmware 2.4.31 EMU (2017-11-10) for the Full HD DVB-S2 satellite receiver on the ALi M3510B / M3503 rev B SoC with 128 MB DDR3 and 8 MB SPI flash.

Uses an XIP CacheAsRam bootloader ("M3510B 1.1.1"), dual-CPU "M3606 SEE" firmware at 0xA6000200, and a 4-digit CH455 LED front panel on GPIO 135 (SCL) / 134 (SDA).

The application prints "---led 455 attach OK--" and updates the CH455 panel to " on ", initialises its MCAS database and userdb(64+64) from defaultdb(PRC) over SPI, and renders its 1280x720 CLUT8 OSD through GeM36F / GMA layer 0 (without the board's anti-clone security IC it displays the hardware-ID warning dialog).

Amiko Micro HD SE (System ID 10010A88) firmware v.2483 (2020-01-17) for the compact Full HD DVB-S2 satellite receiver on the ALi M3511B / M3503 rev B SoC with 128 MB DDR3 and 8 MB SPI flash.

Uses an XIP CacheAsRam bootloader ("M3511B 1.1.1"), dual-CPU "M3606 SEE" firmware at 0x86000200, an external CH455 4-digit LED / IR sensor eye on GPIO 135 (SCL) / 134 (SDA), and the Amiko 0x60xx remote control table ("necfirst" coding).

The application updates the CH455 panel to " on ", probes the RF front-end sharing GPIO 107 / 110, populates userdb(64+64) from defaultdb(PRC) over SPI, and renders its OSD dialog on the Full HD 1920x1080 CLUT8 G1 layer at 0xB8006A00.

Amiko Mini Combo Extra (System ID 24000A00) EMU firmware v1.0.35 for the compact Full HD H.265/HEVC DVB-S2 + DVB-T2/C combo receiver on the ALi M3526A / C3505 SoC with 256 MB DDR3 and 8 MB SPI flash.

Uses the 256 MB DDR remap (0xB8000220 bit 24, SEE at 0xAE000200), a CH455 4-digit LED panel on GPIO 107 (SCL) / 110 (SDA), and the display engine's Full HD 1920x1080 CLUT8 G1 OSD layer at 0xB8006A00.


## `AMIKO MINI COMBO EXTRA/AMIKO_Mini_Combo_Extra_1.0.46_emu.abs`

* **Box:** Amiko Mini Combo Extra (System ID 24000A00)
* **Type:** DVB-S2 + DVB-T2/C Full HD H.265/HEVC combo satellite, terrestrial and cable receiver with Conax / MultiCAS card reader, Ethernet and USB
* **Board:** 24000A00 (bootloader version "3526A 1.1.1", 256 MB DDR3 C3505 platform)
* **SoC:** ALi M3526A / C3505 (256 MB DDR3 dual-CPU H.265/HEVC combo SoC reading chip ID 0x3505; NIM_C3505_0, NIM_COFDM_0, NIM_QAM_S3202, DMX_S3601_0/2, DECV_HEVC_0, DECV_AVC_0, DECV_AVS_0, DECV_S3601_0, OSD_DEV_0/1/2, seecode "M3606 SEE" at 0xAE000200; SDK4.0ia.17.8_20161212byD17CRB) (C3505 (chips/c3505.py))

* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes, panel ' ON ' -> ' on '. The application updates the CH455 panel to " on ", probes the RF front-end sharing GPIO 107 / 110 (M3031 at 0x20, AV2018 at 0x62, demod at 0x14), populates userdb(64+64) from defaultdb(PRC) over SPI, configures the display engine's Full HD 1920x1080 CLUT8 G1 layer at 0xB8006A00 (DMA register-list channel 0x6088, 256-entry ARGB8888 palette at 0x6AEC), and without the board's anti-clone security IC displays "SW is not designed for this HW, please change back to offical SW!-----00000000000000 24000a00".

The application updates the CH455 panel to " on ", populates userdb(64+64) from defaultdb(PRC) over SPI, and renders its 1280x720 OSD dialog on GMA layer 0.

Amiko Mini HD RE (System ID 10000A88) firmware 2.4.33 EMU (2017-11-29) for the Full HD DVB-S2 satellite receiver on the ALi M3511A / M3503 rev B SoC with 128 MB DDR3 and 8 MB SPI flash.

Uses an XIP CacheAsRam bootloader ("M3511A 1.1.1"), dual-CPU "M3606 SEE" firmware at 0xA6000200, and a 4-digit CH455 LED front panel on GPIO 135 (SCL) / 134 (SDA).

## `CABLETECH URZ0083/URZ0083_v1.1.2.abs`

* **Box:** Cabletech URZ0083
* **Type:** DVB-T HD receiver (2011)
* **Board:** MC6238 (the change list's "J1100223_MC6238_URZ0083_v1.0.18")
* **SoC:** ALi M3601E (M3602 (chips/m3602.py))
* **Demodulator:** ALi M3100, external (Gutek's review; the firmware's NIM_COFDM driver tables name the M3101)
* **Flash:** 2 MB SPI
* **IR coding:** ext00
* **Image:** update, V1.1.2 (maincode "Demo M3606" 2011-10-12), 2011-10-12, 2097152 bytes, SHA-1 d709969c2df20a0a8d1e802fb7af000379c02fcb
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000 (DVBT---0.1.0, 2010-06-01), HDCPKey 0x00FE00 (Demo s3602, 2009-11-10), maincode 0x010000 (Demo M3606, 2011-10-12), Radioback 0x160000 (1.0.0, 2009-05-08), countryband 0x170000 (1.0.0, 2010-4-1), userdb 0x18FF80 (1.0.0, 2011-10-12)
* **Source:** [gutek.com.pl](https://www.gutek.com.pl/pobierz/softy/urz0083/v112.rar), Lechpol (Cabletech / Kruger&Matz), mirrored by Gutek (2026-10-10). Gutek's firmware list (https://www.gutek.com.pl/tunery_oprog_do_tunerow.htm), the archive v112.rar; downloaded on 2026-10-10
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes. With its board's chip ID 0x3603 (device.chipId, 2026-10-13) it boots and draws: the bootloader reads the flash with the quad I/O read 0xEB, the application decodes its boot logo (the video engine's completion and the video output's field interrupts, video_m36.py) and shows its first-install wizard in Polish ("Welcome": Region Poland, Język polski, Typ, Wymiary, Tak) within 130 M instructions (run_dump_urz0083_capture_screen.py).  Before (as 0x3602): As the M3602 family (chip ID 0x3602, 2026-10-10): its application starts ("Application version 1.0.0@SDK4.0ba.5.0_GLS_T_64M_20110510") but started over every ~38 M instructions -- its bootloader pulses bit 31 of the chip ID word (0xB6020000, 0x36020000, ...), which, kept, made the application read the chip as 0xB602 and its display driver's attach (0x8027CED8) reboot it.  With the chip ID word read-only (2026-10-13) it runs on: it asks the tuner at I2C 0x60 for its ID (MaxLinear register 0xD3 through the 0xFB prefix; 0x41 = MxL5007T, 0x801C20B8) and the M3101 demodulator at 0x20 (8-bit 0x40) for its registers -- with no chip answering there it waits at that point; with a register file at 0x20 the driver's init runs through (its I2C gateway, the tuner's set-up behind it, reset bit 3 of register 0x01) and then polls register 0x04 for lock.  About 85 M instructions in -- after a byte-by-byte scan of a flash area through its storage driver -- the application shows its boot logo: it writes the logo chunk (0x02FD0100, 0x4DA5 bytes) into the MPEG decoder's buffer twice, and the decoder (DECV_S3601_0) parses it, programs the video engine (0xB8004200: quantiser tables, buffer pointers, 45 x 36 macroblocks) and starts it (+0x14 = 0x200000F).  It then polls the decoder (io_control 5, 0x80002A9C) until the first picture has been shown -- bit 3 of the driver's state word (+0xE0C), which the frame-request callback it hands the video output driver (0x802B2A78) sets.  It waited there for ever while neither the video engine's completion nor the video output's interrupts were modelled; once they were, under 0x3602 its USB host start ran into its assertion right after the logo (an SDBBP, then a jump to 0).

## `CABLETECH URZ0083Q/Cabletech URZ0083Q/EN25Q32B.bin`

* **Box:** Cabletech URZ0083Q
* **Type:** DVB-T receiver
* **Board:** 6390-M3801-VER1.0
* **SoC:** ALi M3801 (M3801)
* **Demodulator:** internal (NIM_S3811)
* **Tuner:** MaxLinear MxL603 family at I2C 0x60 on the first hardware I2C master: the application writes the MxL603 register table at start (3.7 M instructions in), the Cabletech URZ0194S's sequence
* **Flash:** eFeon Q32B-104HIP (read by the programmer as EN25Q32B; 4 MB SPI)
* **Front panel:** TM1628-class 3-wire (CLK 31, DIO 9, STB 11)
* **IR coding:** necfirst
* **Image:** dump, maincode "URZ0083Q" 2013-4-2, 2013-04-02, 4194304 bytes, SHA-1 b417d177a667d3540c335031401e68eeb2b63a27
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000, HDCPKey 0x01FE00 ("Demo M3801"), maincode 0x020000, Radioback 0x320000, defaultdb 0x330000, userdb 0x34FF80 -- the dump.bin layout
* **Source:** [elektroda.pl](https://www.elektroda.pl/rtvforum/topic2842886.html#13677891), Fairgrounds (2014-05-14) -- login needed. Thread "CABLETECH URZ0083Q Wsad pamięci EFEON Q32B-104HIP", post #1 ("zgrane ze sprawnego dekodera" = read from a working decoder): attachment "CABLETECH URZ0083Q.RAR" (4.74 MB) with this image, INFO.txt and two board photos (the photos are not kept in git)
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes, panel ' ON ' -> 'noCH'. Scans its flash channel database for 12-17 minutes, then draws its first-install wizard (run_dump_cabletech_capture_screen.py); the 3-wire panel reads " ON " at boot and "noCH" without channels, and its wizard reacts to the panel's keys.  Its remote (2026-10-14): the IR driver (on the URZ0083Q the HSR 0x80237E50, the NEC decoder 0x80245734, which checks no complement byte) sends every frame on as a key press and a release, and the key task keeps (code >> 24) << 8 | (code & 0xFF) of the received code -- the "necfirst" coding.  The "plain" coding chosen on 2026-10-06 gave MENU, 0x0017, the same frame (rev8(~0x17) = 0x17) but every other key a wrong code (DOWN 0x0037 as 0x0013), so only MENU worked.  On its wizard the remote's DOWN / UP move the highlight and RIGHT steps the value (the language list).

Cabletech URZ0083Q DVB-T receiver on the ALi M3801 (PCB 6390-M3801-VER1.0), read from a working decoder.

INFO.txt in the same folder gives the flash part and the PCB marking.

Before (as 0x3602): As the M3602 family (2026-10-12): the bootloader starts the SEE co-processor -- chips/see.py runs its boot code at 0xA1E8D688, which copies the SEE's program into place, sets the started flag and parks the SEE -- prints "success!" and starts the application, which starts the SEE's program at 0xA6000200 on the second core (see.SeeCore) and attaches its drivers through 63 remote calls the SEE answers (and 18 of the SEE's, which the main CPU answers), printing its register dump; no GE command within 60 M instructions.

Cabletech URZ0086 firmware V1.0.7, the manufacturer's USB update image as Gutek's site mirrors it (urz0086_v107.rar); the archive also holds the update instructions (the box's menu: Narzędzia / Aktualizacja oprogramowania przez USB, the file chosen under "Allcode") and the change list.

Despite the .abs name it is a complete flash image: the ALi chunk chain from offset 0 -- bootloader 0x000000 (DVBS2---0.1.0, 2011-04-14), HDCPKey 0x01FE00 (Demo s3602, 2011-04-14), maincode 0x020000 (M3606 2Tuner, 2011-7-16), seecode 0x140000 (M3606 SEE, 2011-7-16), Radioback 0x240000 (1.0.0, 2011-04-14), countryband 0x250000 (1.0.0, 2011-04-14), userdb 0x26FF80 (1.0.0, 2011-7-16); the maincode's CRC-32/MPEG-2 is intact.  Banners in its LZMA streams: Libcore version 5.0.0@SDK4.0ba.5.0_20110425; Libcore version 1.1.5a@SDK_20100524.

The bootloader chunk's version reads "DVBS2---0.1.0" (ALi's project name) although the box is DVB-T; the maincode is "M3606 2Tuner".  Forum users program these .abs files directly into the flash (renamed .bin): they are complete flash images.

Change list (lista_zmian.txt, Polish): URZ0086_V1.0.7.abs / - soft bazowy

Gutek's review of the URZ0083 and URZ0086 (https://www.gutek.com.pl/tunery_cabletech_urz0083_urz0086_recenzja.htm): the URZ0083 is built on the ALi M3601E with an ALi M3100 demodulator and 64 MB DDR2, the URZ0086 on the ALi M3606 with 128 MB DDR2.  The simulator runs them as the M3602 family (chips/m3602.py).

Its second tuner's I2C bus is bit-banged (2026-10-13): the application drives GPIO 44 (SCL) and 43 (SDA) open-drain and sends the same MaxLinear sequences there (0x60: 0xFF 0x00, 0x02 0x01, reads through the 0xFB prefix) as to the first tuner on the hardware master SCB0 -- the board's two front ends (device.gpioI2c, gpio_i2c.py; no tuner model answers on either yet).

* **Tuner:** MaxLinear MxL101SF at I2C 0x60
* **Flash:** 4 MB SPI
* **IR coding:** nec
* **Image:** update, V1.1.1 (maincode "M3606 2Tuner" 2011-11-15), 2011-11-15, 4194304 bytes, SHA-1 ae41cd38d2d1108d85dfc1e52d84c8b7c90c6558
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000 (DVBS2---0.1.0, 2011-04-14), HDCPKey 0x01FE00 (Demo s3602, 2011-04-14), maincode 0x020000 (M3606 2Tuner, 2011-11-15), seecode 0x140000 (M3606 SEE, 2011-11-15), Radioback 0x240000 (1.0.0, 2011-04-14), countryband 0x250000 (1.0.0, 2011-04-14), userdb 0x26FF80 (1.0.0, 2011-11-15)
* **Source:** [gutek.com.pl](https://www.gutek.com.pl/pobierz/softy/urz0086/urz0086_v111.rar), Lechpol (Cabletech / Kruger&Matz), mirrored by Gutek (2026-10-10). Gutek's firmware list (https://www.gutek.com.pl/tunery_oprog_do_tunerow.htm), the archive urz0086_v111.rar; downloaded on 2026-10-10
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes. With its board's chip ID 0x3603 (device.chipId, 2026-10-13) it boots and draws: the bootloader reads the flash with the quad I/O read 0xEB, the SEE's video drivers decode the boot logo -- video_m36.py's video engine and video output models are wired onto the SEE core and interrupt the core whose controller has the line enabled -- and the SEE's OSD driver draws the first-install wizard in Polish ("Witaj": Region Poland, Język polski, Tryb wyświetlania 576i, Tryb proporcji 4:3LB, Tak) within 230 M instructions.  Until the model read the stream buffer's address right (its bits 24..27 sit in the register's bits 27..30) the engine consumed every bit it was given, and in some runs the SEE stopped at its bit-buffer accounting's assertion (0x860BC008) around 90-100 M instructions.  Before (as 0x3602): As the M3602 family (2026-10-12): the bootloader starts the SEE co-processor -- chips/see.py runs its boot code at 0xA1E8D688, which copies the SEE's program into place, sets the started flag and parks the SEE -- prints "success!" and starts the application, which starts the SEE's program at 0xA6000200 on the second core (see.SeeCore) and attaches its drivers through 63 remote calls the SEE answers (and 18 of the SEE's, which the main CPU answers), printing its register dump; no GE command within 60 M instructions.  Further on (2026-10-13) it creates its OSD region (CLUT8, 568 x 512 at 76, 32) and draws 5 GE commands by ~85 M, when two things stop it: (1) the SEE's MPEG decoder read its VLD bit offset (0xB8004228) back with bits 8..25 cleared by the M3801's status-word model and stopped at its read-pointer assertion -- fixed (ChipFamily.ve_status); (2) the application's USB host open (0x801B77CC) asserts (SDBBP) on a controller without a register base: its attach (0x801B7300) gives one only on chip 0x3101 or on 0x3603 (0xB8032000 / 0xB8032400), while sys_ic_get_usb_num says 1 port on any other chip -- so the real board's M3606 reads 0x3603, like the X110TS's.  Under 0x3603, though, its bootloader's chunk check reads all-zero headers ("malloc size: 0", "CRC bad4") although the flash window holds the image: its flash driver's 0x3603 path (the S3602F's, sflash at 0xB802E000; the CPU / DRAM clocks from the strap pins differ) is not modelled yet.

## `CABLETECH_urz0194s_v1_0_8.bin`

* **Box:** Cabletech URZ0194S
* **Type:** DVB-T receiver
* **SoC:** ALi M3801 (M3801)
* **Demodulator:** internal (NIM_S3811)
* **Tuner:** MaxLinear MxL603 family at I2C 0x60 on the first hardware I2C master: the application writes the MxL603 register table at start (3.8 M instructions in: 0xFF=0, 0x14=0x13, 0x6D=0x8A then 0x0A, 0xDF=0x19, 0x45=0x1B, 0xA9=0x59, 0xAA=0x6A, 0xBE=0x4C ... the Strong SRT 8115's sequence), puts the chip in standby (0x12=0) and wakes it again (0x0B and 0x12 set to 1)
* **Flash:** 25Q32FV (4 MB SPI)
* **Front panel:** TM1628-class 3-wire (CLK 31, DIO 9, STB 11)
* **IR coding:** necfirst
* **Image:** dump, 1.0.8 (maincode "URZ0194" 2013-9-16), 2013-09-16, 4194304 bytes, SHA-1 82438d88edcaaf37da8086184c793cb126abe48d
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000 (Libcore 1.1.6, vic.wang, Mon Oct 15 2012 -- the URZ0083Q's build), HDCPKey 0x01FE00 ("Demo M3801"), maincode 0x020000, Radioback 0x320000, defaultdb 0x330000, userdb 0x34FF80 -- the URZ0083Q / dump.bin layout
* **Source:** [elektroda.pl](https://www.elektroda.pl/rtvforum/topic2981605.html#14403424), Krzyś122333 (2015-02-04) -- login needed. Thread "CABLETECH URZ0194S wsad pamięci 25Q32FV", post #1 ("zgrane ze sprawnego dekodera" = read from a working decoder): attachment "CABLETECH_urz0194s_v1_0_8.bin"
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes, panel ' ON ' -> '----' -> 'noCH'. The application (Libcore 8.1j.0@SDK4.0bd.8.1j_20130424) prints its banner 8 s after start, scans its flash channel database for about 11 minutes and then draws the same first-install wizard as the URZ0083Q (run_dump_urz0194s_capture_screen.py).  Its remote (2026-10-14): the IR driver (on the URZ0083Q the HSR 0x80237E50, the NEC decoder 0x80245734, which checks no complement byte) sends every frame on as a key press and a release, and the key task keeps (code >> 24) << 8 | (code & 0xFF) of the received code -- the "necfirst" coding.  The "plain" coding chosen on 2026-10-06 gave MENU, 0x0017, the same frame (rev8(~0x17) = 0x17) but every other key a wrong code (DOWN 0x0037 as 0x0013), so only MENU worked.  Its MENU opens the main menu and DOWN / UP move through its pages.

The firmware's chip-ID table is the M3801 family's and its demodulator driver is the S3811's.  Its bootloader's standby wake code 00FDBA45 is the URZ0083Q's too, so the same remote: a newer application on the URZ0083Q's hardware family.

In the simulator (2026-10-06): the wizard "Witaj" (Region, Język, Tryb Wyświetlania, Proporcje Obrazu, Ok).  Its TM1628-class front panel sits on the URZ0083Q's pins (CLK 31, DIO 9, STB 11) but its digits use the standard 7-segment layout: " ON " at boot, "----" while the application starts, "noCH" (no channels) once the wizard is up.

* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000 (Libcore 1.1.6, vic.wang, Mon Nov 26 2012), HDCPKey 0x04FE00 ("Demo M3801"), maincode 0x050000, Radioback 0x290000, defaultdb 0x2A0000, userdb 0x2BFF80 (2012-12-12) -- the dump_maciej.bin layout with a 0x50000-byte bootloader area

* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes, panel ' ON ' -> '----' -> '0005'. Boots into its application, which plays the first channel of its database ("prog id : 4", TVN, ~86 M instructions) and draws (2026-10-13, run_dump_urz0195_2013_capture_screen.py): its channel banner (channel 5, "Brak informacji", 0 %) ~20 GE commands in, then, when the banner has timed out, the live-TV "Brak sygnału!" (no signal) screen, scaled from the 1080i output (an earlier simulator had seen no graphics-engine command 14 minutes after its banner).  Its uPD16312-class panel is wired and driven like the 2012 firmware's (the same font table): " ON ", "----", then the channel number "0005" (2026-10-14, checked by the test); it polls 4 key bytes, but its UI's key map (58 entries) holds remote keys only, so no panel key can do anything.  Its remote takes the 2012 firmware's extended-NEC coding (ext00; under the default "nec" neither OK nor DOWN did anything): OK on live TV opens the channel list, DOWN moves its highlight (2026-10-14).

The newer of the two URZ0195 dumps in this repository (the other is urz0195_full_dump(ESMTF25L3204).bin, with an older firmware).  The forum names the chip in later threads about this model; the firmware's chip-ID table is the M3801 family's.

UART log in the simulator (2026-10-05): the bootloader prints its panel configuration ("stb: 14 clock: 31 data: 9", "nec 16312 attach ok", "digit: 4 seg: 16 data_count: 8" -- a uPD16312-class 3-wire LED driver on GPIO 14 / 31 / 9), then bl_flash_init!, bl_verify_sw, check_program!, success!, and the application prints its banner: Libcore version 8.1c.0@SDK4.0bd.8.7_20121127 (the same Libcore build as dump.bin's application), Application version 1.0.0@SDK4.0bd.8.7_20121127byAdministrator.

Simulator run with the 16312 decoder (tm1628_decoder.py on CLK 31 / DIO 9 / STB 14): the bootloader sends 87, 40, C0 + 8 zero bytes, 41 FD (LED port), 08, 40, 8F, then C0 00 00 EE 00 CE 00 00 00 (two digits lit; this chip's segment wiring is not mapped yet, so the decoded text is wrong), and the application repeats the sequence.  14 minutes after the banner (178k timer ticks) it had issued no graphics-engine command yet; an earlier run jumped to address 0 after 13 minutes (the simulator's known asynchronous-stop race).


## `dump.bin`

* **Box:** Comsat TE 1050 HD
* **Type:** DVB-T HD receiver
* **Board:** MC6379-VER1.0
* **SoC:** ALi M3801 (M3801)
* **Demodulator:** internal (NIM_S3811)
* **Tuner:** MaxLinear MxL603 family, by its wake-up: at start the application sets registers 0x0B and 0x12 of a chip at I2C 0x60 to 1 (the MxL603's tuner-enable and start-tune registers), exactly what the Strong SRT 8115's and Cabletech URZ0195's firmwares do before their first tune writes the MxL603 table; this firmware never tunes without channels, so the table itself was not seen
* **Flash:** 25Q32BSIG (4 MB SPI)
* **Front panel:** two buttons straight on GPIO inputs, no LED driver (keys on GPIO 31 / 9)
* **IR coding:** ext00
* **Image:** dump, DVB-T HD V1.1.5 (maincode "M3801 DVBT" 2013-2-1), 2013-02-01, 4194304 bytes
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000 (Libcore 1.1.6, vic.wang, Mon Nov 26 2012), HDCPKey 0x01FE00 ("Demo M3801"), maincode 0x020000, Radioback 0x320000, defaultdb 0x330000, userdb 0x34FF80
* **Source:** [elektroda.pl](https://www.elektroda.pl/rtvforum/topic4155976.html), p.kaczmarek2 (2025-12). The article "Wnętrze tunera Comsat TE 1050 HD, zgrywanie firmware, format partycji z pamięci Flash" (machine translation: https://www.elektroda.com/news/news4155976.html); the same file is published as https://github.com/openshwprojects/FlashDumps (Sat/Comsat TE 1050 HD/Flash_For_M3801_ALI.bin) and https://github.com/openshwprojects/AliUnpacker (dump.bin), identical git blob 5dc3133c8ce82df79ef28dcd69a727703272334a
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes. The simulator's first target; its application draws its first screen after a long start (run_dump_capture_screen.py: its channel banner, then the "Нет Сигнала!" (no signal) box).  Its two front-panel buttons sit straight on GPIO 31 and 9 -- the SDK's key task sends them on as its virtual keys 12 / 13, up / down -- and are modelled released (gpio_keys.py, 2026-10-11): read as pressed, the simulator's default for an input nothing drives, they hopped it between its two channels (490 and 578 MHz) every 20-50 s, which earlier notes took for its channel change never completing.  The remote works in its library's extended-NEC coding (ir_remote's "ext00", the T650i's, address bytes DF DF): OK opens the channel list, MENU the main menu ("Редактировать Канал"), EPG the programme guide, EXIT closes each -- its decoder keeps the frame's first address byte as the key table code's high byte, so a standard NEC frame of its MENU (0xFBDD) was looked up as 0x04DD (traced 2026-10-11), and the buttons' channel hopping had hidden every attempt before.  With the demultiplexer model and a transport stream (2026-10-11, sim.attach_mux) it filters the TDT, the PMT PID of its channel after the PAT (0x6A5 = "TVP Opole" programme 0x11 at 578 MHz, 0x321 = "Polsat Sport News" 0x1A at 490 MHz, from its channel database), then the CAT, SDT, NIT, EIT and the video / audio PIDs, and consumes every packet the model writes.  It sets the chip's real-time clock to the TDT's time (rtc_m36.py, 0xB8018A00; unmodelled it read 0, which the firmware made 28/11 01:00), so its banner shows the stream's date and time and the model's EIT ("10/10 13:00", "Now: 13:00-14:00 TVP Opole now" -- "Нет Информации", no information, when the banner comes before the present event's section -- and "Next: 14:00-15:00 TVP Opole next"; run_dump_signal_capture_screen.py) and times out, the channel staying, a clear black picture; its programme guide then has the two events on its time line.  After the tune it polls the demodulator's state register 0x3B (400 reads in 8 s, wanting 1), 0x147 and, after its init command through 0x12E, the event register 0x02 for a done bit -- all answered by the model with a signal.

p.kaczmarek2's Comsat TE 1050 HD, read with a CH341 programmer for the elektroda article of December 2025 on the box's inside, the firmware read-out and the flash partition format.

The application's system-information page names it "M3801", "MC6379-VER1.0", "TE 1050 HD", "DVB-T HD V1.1.5", "Jan 29 2013".  Application: Libcore 8.1c.0@SDK4.0bd.8.7_20121127.

Tuner: the application initialises the chip's two hardware I2C masters (0xB8018200, 0xB8018700; i2c_scb.py) at start and, on the first, wakes a tuner at I2C address 0x60 (registers 0x0B and 0x12 set to 0x01) -- and nothing more until a channel is tuned, which it never does with its empty channel list; the demodulator is the chip's own (the firmware's "NIM_S3811_0").  The driver names no tuner in its strings (none of the M3801 firmwares does); the register table it writes at the first tune would identify the chip.

## `ECHOLINK EL-700 FTA/flash ECHOLINK EL700FTA mx29lv160.bin`

* **Box:** Echolink EL-700 FTA
* **Type:** DVB-S FTA SD satellite receiver (Moresat "Alpha" / Ali 3329C B-series, 2007)
* **Board:** SMT01 (Eurosat 3023 / Echolink EL-700 FTA)
* **SoC:** ALi M3329C (M3327 / M3329 platform, 216 MHz fixed clock; bootloader "SMT01---0.9.6") (M3329 (chips/m3329.py), matched by bootloader chunk ID 0xE3000010)
* **Demodulator:** internal DVB-S (NIM_M3327; maincode XTEA-encrypted)
* **Tuner:** unknown (on bit-banged GPIO I2C SCL 10 / SDA 9; maincode XTEA-encrypted)
* **Flash:** 2 MB parallel NOR (Macronix MX29LV160, 8-bit bus via STO_FLASH_0)
* **Front panel:** SMTM51 (PAN_SMTM51_0 8051 front-panel & security MCU over SCI_16550_1 UART2 at 0xB8001400, 9600 baud)
* **IR coding:** nec
* **Image:** dump, 1.3.2 (maincode "1.3.2" 2007-1-8; bootloader "SMT01---0.9.6" 2006-12-7), 2007-01-08, 2097152 bytes, SHA-1 329f883b97e62c33c7e2a4cfe19a8389749bfcf7
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000 (SMT01---0.9.6, 2006-12-7), maincode 0x010000 (1.3.2, 2007-1-8, "CODE" XTEA+LZMA), CAS_data 0x08FF80 (1.0.0), ScriptGUI 0x0A0000 (1.0.0), Radioback 0x0B0000 (1.0.0), defaultdb 0x0C0000 (1.0.0), userdb 0x0EFF80 (1.0.0)
* **Source:** [satedu.cba.pl](http://www.satedu.cba.pl/index.php?action=downloadfile&filename=Dump%20ECHOLINK-700%20EUROSAT3023.rar&directory=J-Tag_Dump_Flash) (2026-11-01). JTAG parallel NOR flash dump from archive Dump ECHOLINK-700 EUROSAT3023.rar in J-Tag_Dump_Flash on satedu.cba.pl.
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application no, display no, panel ' on ' -> 'upg '. The bootloader runs (run_dump_el700_security_mcu.py): it configures SDRAM, unpacks "SMT01---0.9.6" to 0x80300000, identifies the 2 MB MX29LV160 parallel NOR flash via AMD autoselect, opens SCI_16550_0 (0xB8001300, 115200 baud) and SCI_16550_1 (0xB8001400, 9600 baud, IC line 6), displays " on " on PAN_SMTM51_0, and sends four 8-byte challenge requests (92 d0 7c 93 b8 74 f7 d5) to the external SMTM51 MCU to obtain the secret half of the 128-bit XTEA key for the "CODE"-wrapped maincode.  Without the proprietary MCU's secret key reply (0x11 0x0A ...), it cleanly aborts decryption, displays "upg " on the front panel, and enters its RS-232 recovery prompt ("\r\n>:") on UART1.

2 MB Macronix MX29LV160 JTAG parallel NOR flash dump of an Echolink EL-700 FTA (also sold as Eurosat 3023), a 2007 DVB-S FTA satellite receiver built on Moresat's "SMT01" / "Alpha" ALi M3329C platform.

Chunk chain: bootloader 0x000000 (chunk ID 0xE3000010, version "SMT01---0.9.6", 2006-12-7), maincode 0x010000 (0x01FE0101, length 0x07EC41, version "1.3.2", 2007-1-8), CAS_data 0x08FF80, ScriptGUI 0x0A0000, Radioback 0x0B0000, defaultdb 0x0C0000 and userdb 0x0EFF80 (1 MB).

Unlike standard ALi M3329 images whose maincode payload is a raw LZMA stream, Moresat wraps the maincode payload (0x010080) in a "CODE" container: the 4-byte magic "CODE" (43 4f 44 45), the big-endian encrypted length 0x0007EBC9, and 519,113 bytes of XTEA-encrypted LZMA data.  The relocated bootloader at 0x80300000 (0x8030D7A8) holds a 16-byte seed at 0x8030EED4 (92 d0 7c 93 b8 74 f7 d5 | 7a 91 51 5a 55 40 1e 11) and sends the first 8 bytes four times over SCI_16550_1 (UART2 at 0xB8001400, 9600 baud, interrupt line 6) to the external 8051 front-panel and anti-clone MCU (PAN_SMTM51_0) in checksummed frames (0d 0a 00 00 92 d0 7c 93 b8 74 f7 d5 80).  Only when the MCU replies with a 0x11 0x0A response carrying 8 secret bytes R[0..7] does 0x8030D87C combine R[0..7] and nibble-swapped R[0..7] XORed into bytes 8..15 to form the 128-bit XTEA key (0x8030D980) before calling LzmaDecode() (0x803058C8) into 0x80000200.

Without the external SMTM51 MCU's secret response (an ACK-only stand-in acknowledges each frame with 0x80 on UART2 RX so link-layer retries do not stall), 0x8030D7A8 returns 0 without running XTEA or jumping into empty RAM; the bootloader then switches PAN_SMTM51_0 from " on " to "upg " and prints its RS-232 serial upgrade prompt "\r\n>:" on UART1 (0xB8001300).

## `ECHOLINK EL-700 FTA/sw_v1.3.7_061108_2.bin`

* **Box:** Echolink EL-700 FTA
* **Type:** DVB-S FTA SD satellite receiver (Moresat "Alpha" / Ali 3329C B-series, 2007)
* **Board:** SMT01 (Eurosat 3023 / Echolink EL-700 FTA)
* **SoC:** ALi M3329C (M3327 / M3329 platform, 216 MHz fixed clock; bootloader "SMT01---0.9.6") (M3329 (chips/m3329.py))
* **Demodulator:** internal DVB-S (NIM_M3327; maincode XTEA-encrypted)
* **Tuner:** unknown (on bit-banged GPIO I2C SCL 10 / SDA 9; maincode XTEA-encrypted)
* **Flash:** 2 MB parallel NOR (Macronix MX29LV160, 8-bit bus via STO_FLASH_0)
* **Front panel:** SMTM51 (PAN_SMTM51_0 8051 front-panel & security MCU over SCI_16550_1 UART2 at 0xB8001400, 9600 baud)
* **IR coding:** nec
* **Image:** dump, 1.3.7 (maincode "1.3.7"; bootloader "SMT01---0.9.9"), 2008-6-11, 2031616 bytes, SHA-1 80ec9000072d4d7bf413577d9294f58b5f44b6ba
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000 (SMT01---0.9.9, 2007-10-11), maincode 0x010000 (1.3.7, 2008-6-11, "CODE" XTEA+LZMA), CAS_data 0x08FF80 (1.0.0, 2007-12-6), ScriptGUI 0x0A0000 (1.0.0, 2006-8-31), Radioback 0x0B0000 (1.0.0, 2006-7-11), defaultdb 0x0C0000 (1.0.2, 2008-5-26), userdb 0x0EFF80 (1.0.0, 2008-6-11)
* **Source:** [satedu.cba.pl](http://www.satedu.cba.pl/index.php?action=downloadfile&filename=Dump%20ECHOLINK-700%20EUROSAT3023.rar&directory=J-Tag_Dump_Flash) (2026-11-01). Archive sw_v1.3.7_061108_2.bin from ECHOLINK EL-700 FTA; added for expanded coverage.
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application no, display no, panel ' on ' -> 'upg '. The bootloader runs (run_dump_el700_security_mcu.py): it configures SDRAM, unpacks "SMT01---0.9.6" to 0x80300000, identifies the 2 MB MX29LV160 parallel NOR flash via AMD autoselect, opens SCI_16550_0 (0xB8001300, 115200 baud) and SCI_16550_1 (0xB8001400, 9600 baud, IC line 6), displays " on " on PAN_SMTM51_0, and sends four 8-byte challenge requests (92 d0 7c 93 b8 74 f7 d5) to the external SMTM51 MCU to obtain the secret half of the 128-bit XTEA key for the "CODE"-wrapped maincode.  Without the proprietary MCU's secret key reply (0x11 0x0A ...), it cleanly aborts decryption, displays "upg " on the front panel, and enters its RS-232 recovery prompt ("\r\n>:") on UART1.

2 MB Macronix MX29LV160 JTAG parallel NOR flash dump of an Echolink EL-700 FTA (also sold as Eurosat 3023), a 2007 DVB-S FTA satellite receiver built on Moresat's "SMT01" / "Alpha" ALi M3329C platform.

Chunk chain: bootloader 0x000000 (chunk ID 0xE3000010, version "SMT01---0.9.6", 2006-12-7), maincode 0x010000 (0x01FE0101, length 0x07EC41, version "1.3.2", 2007-1-8), CAS_data 0x08FF80, ScriptGUI 0x0A0000, Radioback 0x0B0000, defaultdb 0x0C0000 and userdb 0x0EFF80 (1 MB).

Unlike standard ALi M3329 images whose maincode payload is a raw LZMA stream, Moresat wraps the maincode payload (0x010080) in a "CODE" container: the 4-byte magic "CODE" (43 4f 44 45), the big-endian encrypted length 0x0007EBC9, and 519,113 bytes of XTEA-encrypted LZMA data.  The relocated bootloader at 0x80300000 (0x8030D7A8) holds a 16-byte seed at 0x8030EED4 (92 d0 7c 93 b8 74 f7 d5 | 7a 91 51 5a 55 40 1e 11) and sends the first 8 bytes four times over SCI_16550_1 (UART2 at 0xB8001400, 9600 baud, interrupt line 6) to the external 8051 front-panel and anti-clone MCU (PAN_SMTM51_0) in checksummed frames (0d 0a 00 00 92 d0 7c 93 b8 74 f7 d5 80).  Only when the MCU replies with a 0x11 0x0A response carrying 8 secret bytes R[0..7] does 0x8030D87C combine R[0..7] and nibble-swapped R[0..7] XORed into bytes 8..15 to form the 128-bit XTEA key (0x8030D980) before calling LzmaDecode() (0x803058C8) into 0x80000200.

Without the external SMTM51 MCU's secret response (an ACK-only stand-in acknowledges each frame with 0x80 on UART2 RX so link-layer retries do not stall), 0x8030D7A8 returns 0 without running XTEA or jumping into empty RAM; the bootloader then switches PAN_SMTM51_0 from " on " to "upg " and prints its RS-232 serial upgrade prompt "\r\n>:" on UART1 (0xB8001300).

* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes, panel ' O  ' -> ' On ' -> ' on ' -> 'StAr' -> 'nenu'. Boots as a 256 MB DDR3 C3505 board (chips/c3505.py, run_dump_a255s_app_starts.py, run_dump_a255s_capture_screen.py): its boot-ROM bootloader runs in boot SRAM at 0x9FE00800 while reading the chunk table through the 0xAFC00000 flash window, unpacks maincode to 0x80000200 and seecode to 0xAE000200 (224 MB physical DDR), then sets 0xB8000220 bit 24 before jumping to maincode -- switching physical 0x0F000000..0x0FFFFFFF from the flash window to the top 16 MB of DDR (240..256 MB, used for video/GMA buffers) and restoring 0xBFE00000..0xBFEFFFFF to the 0xBF800000..0xBFFFFFFF 8 MB flash mirror.  The application moves EBase to 0x80002000, starts the SEE co-processor at 0xAE000200 (EBase 0x8E002001), initialises the internal S3505 DVB-S2 demodulator + RDA Microelectronics RDA5816 tuner (0x0C on SCB1) and the external Availink AVL6862 DVB-T2/C demodulator (0x14 on SCB3 at 0xB8018D00) + Rafael Micro R840 tuner (0x1A on SCB3), drives the FD650K front panel on GPIO 107 / 108 (" O  ", " On ", " on ", "StAr", "nenu"), and renders its 1280x720 ARGB8888 "System Setup" OSD menu through the display engine at 0xB8006900.

Ferguson Ariva 255 Combo S (Slim) official EU firmware V1.30B4 (2023-11-03) for the Full HD H.265/HEVC 10-bit DVB-S2 + DVB-T2/C CI+ combo receiver on the ALi C3505 SoC with 256 MB DDR3.

Compared with the 2020 HASG1 Ariva 255 Combo board (ALi M3031 at 0x20 + Rafael Micro R836 at 0x3A), the 2023 HASG4 Ariva 255 Combo S board replaces the RF front-ends with an RDA Microelectronics RDA5816 DVB-S2 silicon tuner at I2C 0x0C on SCB1 and a Rafael Micro R840 DVB-T2/C silicon tuner at I2C 0x1A on SCB3 alongside the Availink AVL6862 demodulator at 0x14.

Boots as a 256 MB DDR3 C3505 board (chips/c3505.py, run_dump_a255_app_starts.py, run_dump_a255_capture_screen.py): its boot-ROM bootloader runs in boot SRAM at 0x9FE00800 while reading the chunk table through the 0xAFC00000 flash window, unpacks maincode to 0x80000200 and seecode to 0xAE000200 (224 MB physical DDR), then sets 0xB8000220 bit 24 (0xB8000223 bit 0) before jumping to maincode -- switching physical 0x0F000000..0x0FFFFFFF from the flash window to the top 16 MB of DDR (240..256 MB, used for video/GMA buffers) and restoring 0xBFE00000..0xBFEFFFFF to the 0xBF800000..0xBFFFFFFF 8 MB flash mirror so SYS_FLASH_BASE_ADDR = 0xBFC00000 sees the whole SPI image.  The application moves EBase to 0x80002000, starts the SEE co-processor at 0xAE000200 (EBase 0x8E002001), initialises the internal S3505 DVB-S2 demodulator + ALi M3031 tuner (0x20 on SCB1) and the external Availink AVL6862 DVB-T2/C demodulator (0x14 on SCB3 at 0xB8018D00) + Rafael Micro R836 tuner (0x3A), drives the FD650K front panel on GPIO 107 / 108 (" O  ", " On ", " on ", "StAr", "nenu"), and renders its 1280x720 ARGB8888 "System Setup" OSD menu through the display engine at 0xB8006900.

Ferguson Ariva 255 Combo official firmware V1.32B4 (2020-12-24) for the Full HD H.265/HEVC 10-bit DVB-S2 + DVB-T2/C CI+ combo receiver on the ALi C3505 SoC with 256 MB DDR3.

Unlike the 128 MB C3505 Ariva 104 / 204 / 154 Combo / 254 Combo / T760i builds (SEE at 0xA6000200, flash at 0xAFC00000), the Ariva 255 Combo places its SEE program at 0xAE000200, remaps 0x0F000000..0x0FFFFFFF to DDR via 0xB8000220 bit 24, reads flash from 0xBF800000..0xBFFFFFFF (SYS_FLASH_BASE_ADDR 0xBFC00000), and talks to an Availink AVL6862 / AVL6762 DVB-T2/C demodulator on the C3505's fourth I2C master SCB3 (0xB8018D00).


## `FERGUSON ARIVA 52E/A52E_20160812_V1.31B2.abs`

* **Box:** Ferguson Ariva 52E
* **Type:** DVB-S2 HD satellite receiver with Ethernet, USB recording and internet apps (2015)
* **SoC:** ALi M3606-class dual-CPU chip (the main code's strings name the M3601E / M3606 platform, the seecode chunk is the SEE's program; Application SDK4.0ba.7.20_SAB_S2_20130314) (M3602 (chips/m3602.py), matched by the bootloader chunk's version "37019-01047"; chip ID 0x3603 (chipId))
* **Demodulator:** internal DVB-S2 (NIM_S3501_0, the main code's names)
* **Tuner:** unknown (the main code carries an nim_av7306 driver)
* **Flash:** 8 MB SPI
* **Front panel:** PT6964 (TM1628-class 3-wire) (CLK 65, DIO 66, STB 64)
* **IR coding:** nec
* **Image:** update, V1.31B2 (maincode "V1.31B2*" 2016-08-12; bootloader HSJ2 37019-01047, Libcore 1.1.6@Auto_20100413), 2016-08-12, 8388608 bytes, SHA-1 d28c333e55ae4aed035fa82ff64a6e488df6efc4
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000 (HSJ2 37019-01047, 2015-01-27), maincode 0x020000 (V1.31B2*, 2016-08-12), seecode 0x3E0000 (V1.31B2), radioback 0x540000, ARIVA52E 0x560000 (logo), seeback 0x57FF80, data1 0x590000, data2 0x5A0000, defaultdb 0x680000, userdb 0x6DFF80
* **Source:** [ferguson-digital.eu (the manufacturer's download area)](https://ferguson-digital.eu/download/dvb-s/series_Ariva/Ariva_52E/firmware/A52E_20160812_V1.31B2.zip), Ferguson (2026-10-31). Archive A52E_20160812_V1.31B2.zip from the Ariva 52E firmware directory of Ferguson's download area (with the change list and the upgrade instructions in Polish, English and German); fetched 2026-10-31.
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application no, display no. The bootloader runs (run_dump_a52e_security_ic.py): it prints "APP  init!", parks the SEE through its boot code at 0xA1E90D60, writes the PT6964 panel and unpacks the SEE's program, then has the board's security IC (I2C 0x62 on GPIO 62 / 63) decrypt the first 1 KB of the main code in 64 blocks of 16 bytes.  That chip is not modelled -- its key and cipher are not known --, so LzmaDecode() gets an empty buffer, nothing is unpacked and the jump to 0x80000200 lands in empty RAM (on Unicorn a native crash in the run of zero words; on the C++ engine the CPU slides on to the SEE program's copy at 0x81A00200).  No application, no OSD.

Ferguson Ariva 52E firmware V1.31B2 (2016-08-12), the manufacturer's USB update image (an 8 MB all-code image: the update menu's "Allcode"); the same firmware family covers the Ariva 102E (bootloader HS17), 150 Combo (HS1C) and 250 Combo, and an older V1.27B9 (2015-10-12) is in the same directory as a .7z.

Chunk chain: bootloader 0x000000 ("HSJ2", version 37019-01047, its chunk header's CRC field reads "NCRC"), maincode 0x020000 (3.4 MB), seecode 0x3E0000 (the SEE's program, 1.1 MB, LZO1X-packed; it runs from 0xA6000200), radioback, the ARIVA52E logo, seeback, data1 / data2, defaultdb and userdb.  The bootloader's strings: "Boot loader: No 6M compress buffer!", "APP  init!", PAN_PT6964_0, STO_SFLASH_0, ota_prog_restore (stored reversed) and Libcore version 1.1.6@Auto_20100413.  The main code names an Airoha-family nim_av7306 tuner driver and the internal S3501 demodulator; the change list mentions multiroom, IPTV and internet apps.

The main code is encrypted at its start, and the decryption is done by a chip on the board: the bootloader sends the main-code chunk's first 1024 bytes, 16 at a time, over a bit-banged I2C bus (SCL = GPIO 62, SDA = GPIO 63, bank 0xB80000D4 bits 30 / 31) to address 0x62 -- each request is 0xC1, the seven bytes bd 29 8c 0b f9 d6 cd, the 16 encrypted bytes and a CRC-16/BUYPASS (polynomial 0x8005, initial 0) of the 24 before it, big-endian -- and reads 26 bytes back.  The bootloader holds no cipher tables (no AES or DES S-box); the encrypted 0xE0 bytes at the start are the same in V1.27B9 and V1.31B2 and in the 102E and 150 Combo images (the same LZMA stream start), and the plaintext is then unpacked with LzmaDecode() to 0x80000200.  Without the chip's answers (no acknowledge: each block is tried nine times) the bootloader carries on with an empty buffer, so the application never starts in the simulator.

Front panel: the 3-wire PT6964 on GPIO bank 2 (0xB80000F4) bits 0..2 -- STB = GPIO 64, CLK = GPIO 65, DIO = GPIO 66 --; the bootloader writes 0x13 0x03 to RAM 2-3 and 0x33 0x03 to RAM 6-7, whose segment wiring is not known (the font is the application's).  The remote's coding is not known either (irCoding "nec" is the default, untested).

The bootloader's progress depends on the slice length: in slices of 100 k instructions it stays in a MIPS16 loop of its own (0x81E868A6..) for more than 60 M instructions, in slices of 500 k and more it reaches the security IC after ~2 M instructions and LzmaDecode() at ~4.5 M (not looked into).

## `FERGUSON ARIVA T50/ArivaT50_20111118_V102B214.abs`

* **Box:** Ferguson Ariva T50
* **Type:** DVB-T HD receiver with USB recording and a media player
* **SoC:** ALi M3602 (the maincode chunk's version reads "Demo M3602": ALi's SDK project) (M3602 (chips/m3602.py))

* **Flash:** 4 MB SPI
* **IR coding:** cmd
* **Image:** update, V1.02B214 (maincode "Demo M3602" 2011-11-18), 2011-11-18, 4194304 bytes, SHA-1 48b9e41aae5f90b0af54f138a42deac7dae18344
* **Layout:** bootloader 0x000000 (DMB01---0.1.0, 2011-11-18), maincode 0x010000 (Demo M3602, 2011-11-18), radioback 0x340000 (1.0.0, 2010-6-25), bootlogo 0x348000 (1.0.0, 2010-6-21), customerradiolo 0x358000 (1.0.0, 2011-8-16), countryband 0x360000 (1.1.0, 2011-11-18), userdb 0x36FF80 (1.0.0, 2011-11-18)
* **Source:** [ferguson-digital.eu](https://ferguson-digital.eu/download/dvb-t/series_Ariva/Ariva_T50/firmware/ArivaT50_20111118_V102B214.zip), Ferguson (2011-11-18). Ferguson's official download area (https://ferguson-digital.eu/download/?dir=dvb-t%2Fseries_Ariva%2FAriva_T50%2Ffirmware): ArivaT50_20111118_V102B214.zip (1.54 MB) also holds a Polish upgrade guide and revision_history.txt (the formats its media player plays); only the .abs image is kept here; downloaded on 2026-10-10
* **Simulator:** boots yes, application yes, display yes. Draws its installation wizard "Welcome" (Region, Language, Display Mode 576i, Aspect Mode Auto, OK) at ~315 M instructions, 91 GE commands; DOWN moves its highlight (run_dump_t50_capture_screen.py, 2026-10-14).  Its OSD is drawn by the M3602's own GE at 0xB800C000 (ge_m3602.py, the SDK's ge_hal.c) into a 912 x 640 CLUT8 screen, which the GE scales through the YCbCr palette into the 513 x 512 AYCbCr8888 layer of its PAL output (layer 1: 0xB80061A0 bit 8, head at 0xB80061AC).  On the way: its video output driver polled the output's status bit 0 (0xB8006004 bit 8) before switching TV systems (video_m36 sets it half a field after each field start); its control task then waited on libpub's event flag for its logo, whose PUB task polls the decoder's VDEC_CB_FIRST_SHOWED callback -- which its decoder, in the dual-output mode (+0xB44 = 8), calls only once the SD output (the DEO at 0xB8020000, interrupt-controller line 15, its field at bit 19) has requested the frame too.  Its remote key table (0x802F2DC4, 63 entries) holds each key's command half only, rev8(command) << 8 | rev8(~command); its control task drops a key unless the received code's high half is 0x803F (0x8000AD0C): extended NEC with the address bytes 0x01, 0xFC (ir_remote coding "cmd").  The M3101 demodulators at I2C 0x20 / 0x21 and the tuner it asks for at 0x63 still do not answer.  Before: with the flash's electronic ID answered as a real 4 MB part answers it (2026-10-13: the last byte of the 0xAB read, 0x15 -- the 2009 bootloader's flash table knows the part by that byte only) its flash driver attaches the flash and the bootloader starts the application: "MC: APP  init ok", Libcore 1.1.6@Auto_20100413, the demultiplexer's and the video decoders' attach messages; it then sets up its two M3101 demodulators at I2C 0x20 / 0x21 and asks for an MxL5007T-type tuner at 0x63 behind them -- nothing answers there -- and polls the first demodulator's lock register; no GE command within 230 M instructions.  Its AppInit completes at ~29 M (it returns at 0x8001D544), but the UI's control task never reaches its key loop (get_key, 0x800099C0, not called after 60 M): no remote frame reaches its key lookup (0x80008C6C), whatever the address, and stand-in demodulators at 0x20 / 0x21 change nothing.  Its key table (0x802F2DC4, 63 entries) is the older layout: each code is the low half of the received NEC code, rev8(command) << 8 | rev8(~command), without the address byte (ir_remote.find_key_table then wanted one shared address byte).  Its video output's interrupt looks up the OSD drivers "OSD_M3327C_0", "OSD_M3327C_1" and "OSD_M3327_0" every field, but no OSD layer is set up in any display block (0xB8006000, 0xB800E000, 0xB8020000) by 120 M.  Before: As the M3602 family (chip ID 0x3602, 2026-10-10): the bootloader prints "APP  init ok" 459 times in 100 M instructions and starts over each time without starting the application.

Ferguson Ariva T50 firmware V1.02B214, the manufacturer's USB update image from Ferguson's download area (ArivaT50_20111118_V102B214.zip).

Despite the .abs name it is a complete flash image: the ALi chunk chain from offset 0 -- bootloader 0x000000 (DMB01---0.1.0, 2011-11-18), maincode 0x010000 (Demo M3602, 2011-11-18), radioback 0x340000 (1.0.0, 2010-6-25), bootlogo 0x348000 (1.0.0, 2010-6-21), customerradiolo 0x358000 (1.0.0, 2011-8-16), countryband 0x360000 (1.1.0, 2011-11-18), userdb 0x36FF80 (1.0.0, 2011-11-18); the maincode's CRC-32/MPEG-2 is intact.  Banners in its LZMA streams: Libcore version 1.1.6@Auto_20100413.

The front-panel driver is "PAN_PT_0" (a PT6964-style shift-register panel in ALi's SDK), not one front_panel.py decodes yet.

The bootloader chunk's version is "DMB01---0.1.0" (its Libcore 1.0.9@Auto_20090520); the chain also carries a boot logo ("bootlogo", an MPEG still) and a "customerradiolo" (the radio-mode background).

The simulator runs it as the M3602 family (chips/m3602.py).

In the simulator (2026-10-10, the M3602 family): the bootloader probes its DDR at 0xA800AA68 (the family shows the RAM again above 128 MB), prints "APP  init ok", identifies the flash (JEDEC EF 40 16), reads it and runs a bitwise CRC (MIPS16 code at 0x806842EA in its RAM copy), and then takes its reset path: $fp = 0xDEADBEAD and the routine at 0x80688C34, which pulses the module resets (0xB8000080 = 0xFFBFFFFF for chip 0x3602; 0x1FF to 0xB8000060 for any other chip ID) and jumps to 0xBFC00000.  The path that starts the application instead sets $fp = 0xDEADBEEF and jumps to the flash entry 0xAFC00000 (0x80688D5C), whose reset code checks for that value.  It was not a failed check: the bitwise loop is the CRC table's set-up, and check_program's first flash read (sto_fetch_long, 0x806845D8) found no flash device and called that reset routine (0x80688D48) -- the flash driver's attach had registered none, as no entry of its table matched the part's IDs (2026-10-13).

The upper 4 MB are reached the SDK way, at 0xAFC00000 - 4 MB + offset (simulator.py _flash_offset).

The application rewrites three sectors in the upper 4 MB at start, resets its Ethernet MAC (ETHERNET_MAC_0, 0xB802C000) and probes the PHY over MDIO (no PHY: reads 0xFFFF), then -- the channel database being empty -- runs the first-install automatic search ("Przeszukiwanie auto", Polish UI, Ferguson's black / orange skin): its progress screen from ~7 min, "nie znaleziono kanału!" (no channel found) with a "tak" button at 100 % after ~18 min (217 GE commands).

The chip reads as revision B (chip word 0x38210001): under revision A the application leaves the GMA to the SEE and its OSD code calls the SEE's device directly, jumping into the SEE's code at ~69 M.  Panel keys (2026-10-14, front_panel._FERGUSON_KEYS): the PAN_FD650K driver switches on the key byte (key - 0x5C, a jump table) and turns DIG1 / DIG2 of KI4..KI7 into the panel codes its UI maps -- KI4/DIG1 down, KI4/DIG2 exit, KI5/DIG1 left, KI5/DIG2 menu, KI6/DIG1 right, KI6/DIG2 power, KI7/DIG1 up, KI7/DIG2 OK.  On the wizard right steps the Region value (resetting the countdown), exit opens the main menu's "Edytuj kanały" page (the panel shows "nenu") and down highlights its first item (run_dump_t750i_capture_screen.py).  Its remote (2026-10-14) takes the T650i's extended-NEC coding (ext00; its key task keeps the code's first address byte): under the default "nec" DOWN did nothing on the first-install wizard, whose countdown then started the channel search; under ext00 DOWN moves the wizard's highlight.  With the transport stream behind a signal on 177.5 MHz (sim.attach_mux, 2026-10-14; its "DMX_S3601_0" driver programs the M3801's DMX0 at 0xB8022000 with single-entry PID filters, dmx_m36.Demux(pid_entries=True)) its automatic search finds "AliSimulator TV" on CH05 (every other channel "... Błąd"), and so does its manual search (panel exit, RIGHT to "Instalacja", OK, OK, three DOWNs to "Szukaj", OK): it stores the channel (panel "OOO1"), asks about the programme guide ("Nie": RIGHT, OK; unanswered it says yes after some seconds, and EXIT leaves the download), plays it -- its banner shows "10/10/2026 14:00" and the stream's "14:00~15:00 AliSimulator TV now" / "15:00~16:00 ... next" -- and its channel list shows "1 AliSimulator TV" and "177500/2K/QPSK" (scratch runs: no regression test, as "STB not signed!" pops up every minute of play, see below).  Its OTP memory (chips/m3821.Otp, 2026-10-14) is blank, as on an unsigned box: every 60 ticks of play the firmware checks the two 64-byte halves of its signature at 0x1C0 / 0x3A0 (0x80016FCC -> 0x8007EB28 on the T750i) and, finding them blank, shows "STB not signed!" for 5 s.  A non-blank stand-in there (tried 2026-10-14) sends its start-up down the signed path -- the signature's RSA check -- where the simulator crashed (Unicorn's long-block fault), so the sidecar gives none.

Ferguson Ariva T750i firmware V1.20B2, the manufacturer's USB update image from Ferguson's download area (T750i_20190918_V1.20B2.zip).

Despite the .abs name it is a complete flash image: the ALi chunk chain from offset 0 -- HAT24 0x000000 (66019-01047, 20150930-172959), HDCPKey 0x01FE00 (1.0.0, 20170502-094524), OTAloader 0x020000 (V1.20B2, 20151112-203754), ota_see 0x0DEE00 (V1.20B2, 20151020-173032), OTAparam 0x10EE00 (1.0.0, 20190918-180159), MemCfg 0x10F000 (00000001, 20190918-180158), maincode 0x110000 (V1.20B2, 20190918-180158), seecode 0x560000 (V1.20B2, 20190918-180158), radioback 0x6D0000 (1.0.0, 20150923-151837), seeback 0x6EFF80 (1.0.0, 20150923-151837), T750i 0x700000 (1.0.0, 20150923-151837), data 0x71FF80 (1.0.0, 20150923-151836), defaultdb 0x770000 (1.0.0, 20150923-151837), userdb 0x78FF80 (1.0.0, 20190918-180159); the maincode's CRC-32/MPEG-2 is intact.  Banners in its LZMA streams: Libcore version 13.6.0@SDK4.0ga.13.6_20141202; Libcore version 1.1.5a@SDK_20111126.

The image carries a second CPU's code: "seecode" (V1.20B2, the SEE -- ALi's secure co-processor -- with its own Libcore 1.1.5a@SDK_20111126), and the image has an OTA loader with its own SEE part ("OTAloader" / "ota_see", Libcore 13.6.0@SDK4.0ga.13.6_20141202), "MemCfg" and a "T750i" chunk (the boot picture).  The R265 Lite's M3822P images have no SEE chunk, so this is the first M3821-family image that needs the SEE CPU's mailbox (or a stand-in for it).

The front panel is an FD650K ("PAN_FD650K", as on the T650i); its GPIO pins are not known yet.

In the simulator (2026-10-10; chips/m3821.py now models all of it but the SEE's program): the bootloader is the M3801 kind -- it runs from the flash window, not from the R265 Lite's boot SRAM -- and takes its M3821 set-up path when the chip ID word says 0x3821.  Until the DDR is up it keeps its stack in locked D-cache lines at 0x8FFF8000..0x8FFFFFFF (cache-as-RAM: it reads that range to load the lines and locks its DDR set-up functions into the I-cache with cache 0x14), so as the default M3801 it pops a return address of 0xFFFFFFFF from flash and ends at PC 0.  With RAM over those 32 KB, the chip word 0x38210000 and the M3821 family's devices it prints "HW BootLoader APP  init!", checks the program ("check_program finish."), unpacks the SEE code (0x57A7A1 -> 0x3370B0 bytes, "run see, see_entry = 0x8132f000!"), writes the SEE's start address 0xA1017804 to 0xB8000200 and waits for bit 0 of 0xB800020C (the SEE has started); with that bit answered it unpacks the main code (0x82EFF8 bytes) and prints "success!".  The application (EBase 0x80002000, its start code picks a set-up by the chip ID: 0x3503, 0x3281, 0x3811, ...) registers handlers for interrupts 0x46 / 0x47 and then waits for five words at 0x808FCF40 to become non-zero -- the SEE's messages -- with its other tasks idle: it needs the SEE CPU running its own code (and the mailbox between the two), which the simulator does not have.  (Fast mode: the bootloader runs its set-up through the flash window's cached view -- its mtc0 EBase to its own vectors at 0x81016000 (flash offset 0x74C) executes at 0x8FC0074C -- so the simulator hooks the flash's CP0 instructions in the KSEG0 views too; with only the KSEG1 views hooked that write ran natively and the bootloader's first interrupt went to an empty 0x80000180.)

As the C3505 family (2026-10-12), like V1.5B4: the boot ROM's step into the boot SRAM, the bootloader waits for bit 8 of 0xB8000300, unpacks the application and starts it; the application moves its exception vectors (EBase 0x80002000) and starts the SEE co-processor's program at 0xA6000200 on the second core (see.SeeCore; it moves its own, EBase 0x86002000), prints its banner and attaches its drivers through remote calls with the newer chips' doorbells (60 answered and 54 of the SEE's by ~76 M instructions); its ATBM7812 demodulator answers its chip ID 0xA8 at I2C 0x40 (demods.py, the sidecar's demodModel; without it the driver retried its power-on init for ~125 M instructions).  Its screen (2026-10-13), like V1.5B4's: the first-install wizard "Welcome" ("OK (10 sec)" counting down) by ~110 M, through the newer display engine's layer at 0xB8006900 (gma_capture.de_layers).  Panel keys (2026-10-14, front_panel._FERGUSON_KEYS): the PAN_FD650K driver switches on the key byte (key - 0x5C, a jump table) and turns DIG1 / DIG2 of KI4..KI7 into the panel codes its UI maps -- KI4/DIG1 down, KI4/DIG2 exit, KI5/DIG1 left, KI5/DIG2 menu, KI6/DIG1 right, KI6/DIG2 power, KI7/DIG1 up, KI7/DIG2 OK.  Its remote (2026-10-14) takes the T650i's extended-NEC coding (ext00; its key task keeps the code's first address byte): under the default "nec" DOWN did nothing on the first-install wizard, whose countdown then started the channel search; under ext00 DOWN moves the wizard's highlight.  Its OTP memory (chips/m3821.Otp, 2026-10-14) is blank, as on an unsigned box: every 60 ticks of play the firmware checks the two 64-byte halves of its signature at 0x1C0 / 0x3A0 (0x80016FCC -> 0x8007EB28 on the T750i) and, finding them blank, shows "STB not signed!" for 5 s.  A non-blank stand-in there (tried 2026-10-14) sends its start-up down the signed path -- the signature's RSA check -- where the simulator crashed (Unicorn's long-block fault), so the sidecar gives none.

The chip is not an M3821: the C3505 is a later ALi generation (a DVB-S2 SoC; here the external AltoBeam ATBM7812 receives DVB-T2), which the simulator runs as chips/c3505.py: the M3821's boot-ROM path with the chip ID 0x3505.

Changelog (changelog.txt, PL / EN): V1.5B4-14092021 -- YouPorn hidden by the "parental lock" function; improved PVR screen keyboard.

* **IR coding:** nec
* **Image:** update, 1.3.5 "Reta_pol" (the Polish retail build: main-code chunk 112003000202162, version 00000135, "POL_NETR_PVR"; Libcore 13.8.0@SDK4.0fa.13.8_20150326, Application 1.0.0@SDK4.0fa.13.8_20150326; the SEE's uLibcore 1.1.5a@SDK_20111126), 2015-06-22, 4194304 bytes, SHA-1 ff739ea839864260bdba590d7f5c076d22504c9a
